lessons.title: Values and Types
lessons.why: Here’s the simple reason this matters: This lesson is about Values and Types. Keep the idea practical: in the plain-JavaScript TaskFlow Lite application, the worked example should show that you see the primitive/value categories JavaScript actually stores; `null` is a value and an unassigned variable is `undefined`. Once you can explain why that happens, the name is much easier to remember. We connect it to the course project so you can see the idea working instead of memorizing a definition.
objectives: Explain Values and Types in terms of inputs, owner, outputs, and failure modes.
Implement Values and Types incrementally and predict observable evidence before execution.
Diagnose a controlled Values and Types failure from evidence.
Apply Values and Types to a new TaskFlow requirement without copying the reference implementation.
prerequisites: Complete the previous lesson in JavaScript Programming — TaskFlow Lite or demonstrate equivalent skill.
Start from a healthy project/checkpoint.
mentalModel: This lesson is about Values and Types. Once you can explain why that happens, the name is much easier to remember.

Now place it in TaskFlow. This lesson belongs to the plain-JavaScript TaskFlow Lite application and the programming ideas React later builds on. Ask four questions while you work: what enters this boundary, who owns the decision, what dependency does it use, and what evidence proves the result?
